historical_commentary.text: This note describes a v6 feature allowing 4D Clients to view and modify variables on other clients without using traditional synchronization mechanisms like fields, semaphores, or disk files. This was a novel capability for the era and reflects the tight client/server architecture of 4D v6. Modern 4D approaches inter-client communication differently, using shared objects and collections (introduced in v16+), server-side stored procedures, or ORDA-based entity locking rather than direct variable sharing across client processes.
